terms.gloss: an example, an instance; a model to follow
evidence: Cic. Phil. 13.2: exemplī causā paucōs nōmināvī
terms.comment: Exemplī causā or grātiā, for example; exemplum dare or praebēre, set an example (Tac., Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: imperative of putō, used as an adverb
evidence: Hor. S. 2.5.32: Quīnte, puta, aut Pūblī (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: a lesson, an example, a warning
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: what teaches, an example or a warning.

phrases.latin: longum iter est per praecepta, breve et efficāx per exempla
phrases.english: the road through rules is long; through examples it is short and effective

phrases.latin: ducēs exemplō potius quam imperiō, sī prōmptī, sī cōnspicuī, sī ante aciem agant, admīrātiōne praesunt
phrases.english: leaders lead by example rather than by command: if they are ready, if they are seen, if they fight in front, they lead because they are admired
I have named a few, by way of example

puta.html: Lewis & Short, s.v. putō: pŭtă, imperative, used for “for example”.

sources: Lewis & Short: exemplum · Lewis & Short: ut · Lewis & Short: puto
